identificationModule.briefTitle: A Clinical Trial of Flonoltinib Maleate for Intermediate or High-Risk Myelofibrosis
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized, Open-label, Positive-controlled, Parallel-grouped, Multicenter Phase III Clinical Trial on the Efficacy and Safety of Flonoltinib Maleate Tablets in Patients With Intermediate- or High-risk Myelofibrosis

leadSponsor.name: Chengdu Zenitar Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This trial adopts a multicenter, open label, positive drug parallel controlled clinical trial design, with a planned enrollment of approximately 105 participants in the MF trial. Successful trial participants were selected and assigned to either the experimental group or the control group in a 2:1 stratified manner, with the stratification factor being the Dynamic International Prognostic Scoring System (DIPSS) prognostic grading criteria. Continuously take the test drug/control drug until it meets the withdrawal criteria.

armGroups.label: Experimental group
armGroups.description: Flonoltinib Maleate Tablets 75mg, taken orally, qd

armGroups.label: control group
armGroups.description: The dosage of Ruxolitinib Phosphate Tablets is based on baseline PLT level according to the label, taken orally, bid

primaryOutcomes.measure: Percentage of subjects with >=35% reduction in spleen volume from baseline

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Spleen response time: The time when the spleen volume is first observed to decrease by >=35% from baseline
MPN-SAF TSS Total Symptom Score and Baseline Comparison Decrease
secondaryOutcomes.description: The MPN-SAF-TSS is used to assess the symptom burden of patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms. The questionnaire also reflects the quality of life of patients to a certain extent. During the diagnosis and treatment process, the MPN-10 questionnaire includes 10 sub symptoms (fatigue, early satiety, abdominal discomfort, poor activity, lack of concentration, night sweats, skin itching, bone pain, fever, and weight loss). Each item is graded from 0 (none) to 10 (heaviest), with a total score of 0-100 points. The higher the total score, the heavier the symptom burden.
The time interval between the first use of medication and death caused by any reason
